title: The Hollow of Highmoor
premise: In the fog-bound city of Highmoor, where magic was outlawed a generation ago, Ada Sterling keeps her guild's last charm-shop alive by selling trinkets with just enough power to warm cold hands. When a stranger named Corin Ash arrives and his name appears in the Hollow Prophecies—a century-old ledger kept beneath the mountain—Ada learns he is the soul her grandmother sold to the court below to buy the guild's survival. To free him before the moon's thirteenth turn, Ada must descend into the Hollow Court, outwit its memory-eating magistrates, and choose between restoring her guild's stolen legacy or saving the man fate wrote down. She burns the prophecy itself, freeing both their futures at the cost of everything the guild once was.
about_author: L. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a drafty attic full of unlabeled keys and insist none of them are magic.

chapters.title: The Shop That Smells of Rain
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In her crumbling charm-shop, Ada sells a luck-knot to a frightened child while hiding the shop's true magic from a city inspector. Establishes her exhaustion, loyalty to the dying guild, and quiet defiance. Emotional beat: weary tenderness—the small warmth she trades in a city that fears wonder.

chapters.title: A Stranger Buys Nothing
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Corin Ash enters at closing time, asks for a charm against being remembered, and leaves without buying. That night Ada finds his face sketched in her grandmother's forbidden ledger beside tomorrow's date. Beat: unease blooming into dread as the past reaches through paper.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada deciphers her grandmother's cipher: the Hollow Prophecies record souls sold to the court beneath Highmoor, and Corin's entry ends in thirteen moons. Her guild's prosperity was bought with his freedom. Beat: guilt—inheritance revealed as theft.

chapters.title: Corin Ash, Unremembered
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Corin explains he has drifted through Highmoor for years; no one recalls meeting him twice. He came to the shop because it was the only door that ever opened twice for him. Beat: lonely recognition—two invisible people seeing each other clearly.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada confronts the last other guild member, old Master Fenwick, who confirms the bargain: one soul per generation, freely given by the guildhead. He begs her to let it stand. Beat: betrayal and the bitter taste of respectability built on a buried crime.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons, Counting Down
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ada and Corin research the Hollow Court in sealed archives, learning that on the thirteenth turn the soul becomes court property forever—and the prophecy names Ada as the next seller. Beat: resolve hardening; the clock begins.

chapters.title: The Inspector's Kind Offer
chapters.summary: Inspector Vael's POV. Vael, who has suspected the shop for years, offers Ada immunity if she informs on the underground remnant guilds. She refuses, and he marks her door. Beat: fear sharpened into open opposition; the law becomes an antagonist.

chapters.title: Doors Beneath the City
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Following Corin's half-remembered dreams, they find a sealed stair beneath the old aqueduct. The stones recognize Corin's name and open. Beat: awe and vertigo—descending from the known world into inheritance's true cellar.

chapters.title: The Market of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the border-hollow between city and court, they trade memories for passage with the ferryman Wren, who remembers everyone but herself. Ada gives up her mother's lullaby. Beat: sacrifice establishing the price of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Magistrates Who Eat Yesterday
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. First sight of the Hollow Court: magistrates who consume memories as evidence, weighing souls like ledgers. Corin learns his sale contract bears his own childhood signature. Beat: horror—he consented once, as a child, not knowing what he signed.

chapters.title: A Bargain Overheard
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hiding in the court's archive, Ada overhears the Chief Magistrate plan to claim her as the next seller when the moon turns, binding the guild's line to the court forever. Beat: stakes escalate from one soul to generations.

chapters.title: The Room Where Grandmother Waited
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada finds her grandmother's preserved memory, stored as evidence. Inside it she witnesses the original sale—her grandmother weeping, believing she saved the guild. Beat: compassion complicating anger; villains were desperate women first.

chapters.title: Wren's Price
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals she was the first sold soul, released incomplete, and has ferried bargainers for a century hoping someone would finish the job. She tells them the contract can be broken only by burning the master prophecy. Beat: hope with teeth—an ally, and a debt.

chapters.title: What Corin Remembers
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Recovering fragments in the archive, Corin recovers his childhood: he chose to be forgotten to spare his village a plague-bargain. His invisibility was mercy, then punishment. Beat: grief transmuted into dignity—he was never nothing.

chapters.title: Vael Follows the Stair
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. Inspector Vael descends after them, driven less by duty than by his own erased brother, sold decades ago. He captures Ada to trade her for his brother's record. Beat: antagonist humanized; the law's enforcer is also its orphan.

chapters.title: Trial by Memory
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The magistrates put Ada on trial, feeding her memories to the court one by one. She fights to keep hold of Corin's face as her past dissolves. Beat: terror and endurance—love as the last thing she refuses to surrender.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. The moon completes its turn; the court begins consuming Corin. Wren rebels, flooding the chamber with stolen memories, buying minutes. Beat: chaos and courage—allies spending themselves without hesitation.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Book
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Freed by Wren's flood, Ada seizes the master prophecy and burns it before the court, unmaking every contract—including her own future entry. The magistrates unravel as their evidence turns to ash. Beat: triumphant defiance—justice done outside any law.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Corin is restored but remembers almost nothing of Ada; the fire took the price with the prize. Vael chooses to falsify his report rather than arrest them, having found his brother's name among the freed. Beat: bittersweet cost—victory that feels like loss.

chapters.title: Relearning a Face
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Back in the shop, Ada decides not to remind Corin who she was, letting him choose anew. He returns anyway, drawn by something warmer than memory. Beat: quiet ache resolving into grace—love beyond the ledger.

chapters.title: The Guild of One
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada reopens the shop openly, magic unhidden, teaching the neighborhood children small wonders. Fenwick arrives ashamed; she offers him apprenticeship, not judgment. Beat: reconciliation—inheritance reclaimed as responsibility, not bloodline.

chapters.title: Highmoor, Remembered
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. On the first anniversary, Wren surfaces with her own name restored, Vael leaves flowers at a door that no longer needs watching, and Corin writes his name in a new book—one that records choices, not fates. Beat: hopeful closure—the hollow filled by what people give freely.
